title: Mark 16 — The Resurrection narrative + the longer-ending textual-critical site (Mark 16:9-20 absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus)

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — earliest substantial manuscript witnesses (Codex Vaticanus B/03 + Codex Sinaiticus א/01, 4th c. CE); SBLGNT base text. Mark 16:9-20 absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bobiensis + Sinaitic Syriac; preserved here per WoH-Translation textual-critical convention with dispute documented in apparatus.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai diagenomenou tou sabbatou Maria hē Magdalēnē kai Maria hē tou Iakōbou kai Salōmē ēgorasan arōmata hina elthousai aleipsōsin auton.

i18n.en: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, so that they might come and anoint him.

paragraphs.text: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου.
paragraphs.translit: kai lian prōi tē mia tōn sabbatōn erchontai epi to mnēmeion anateilantos tou hēliou.

i18n.en: And very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς· Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου;
paragraphs.translit: kai elegon pros heautas· Tis apokylisei hēmin ton lithon ek tēs thyras tou mnēmeiou?

i18n.en: And they were saying to one another, "Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?"

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀποκεκύλισται ὁ λίθος, ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai anablepsasai theōrousin hoti apokekylistai ho lithos, ēn gar megas sphodra.

i18n.en: And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled back; for it was exceedingly great.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν, καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthousai eis to mnēmeion eidon neaniskon kathēmenon en tois dexiois peribeblēmenon stolēn leukēn, kai exethambēthēsan.

i18n.en: And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white robe; and they were amazed.

notes.official: The Markan *neaniskos* (young man) sitting at the right side of the tomb in a white robe is notably NOT identified as an angel (contrast Mt 28:2 *angelos kyriou*; Lk 24:4 *andres dyo en esthēti astraptousē*). The Markan ambiguity is widely-treated as deliberate (Marcus AB 2009; Collins Hermeneia 2007). Cross-reference to Mk 14:51-52 (the *neaniskos* fleeing naked at Gethsemane) has produced an extensive literary-critical discussion of the figure as a Markan-signature literary device (Croy 2003; Magness 1986); the figure is preserved in its Markan-distinctive ambiguity rather than harmonized to the Mt/Lk angelic-figure tradition.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς· Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε· Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· ἠγέρθη, οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: ho de legei autais· Mē ekthambeisthe· Iēsoun zēteite ton Nazarēnon ton estaurōmenon· ēgerthē, ouk estin hōde· ide ho topos hopou ethēkan auton·

i18n.en: And he said to them, "Do not be amazed. You seek Jesus the Nazarene, the crucified one. He has been raised; he is not here. See the place where they laid him.

paragraphs.text: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε, καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: alla hypagete eipate tois mathētais autou kai tō Petrō hoti Proagei hymas eis tēn Galilaian· ekei auton opsesthe, kathōs eipen hymin.

i18n.en: But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going before you into Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you."

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν, ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthousai ephygon apo tou mnēmeiou, eichen gar autas tromos kai ekstasis· kai oudeni ouden eipan, ephobounto gar.

i18n.en: And going out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

notes.official: Mark's original ending (per Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bobiensis + Sinaitic Syriac) closes mid-sentence on the conjunction *gar* — *ephobounto gar* 'for they were afraid'. Modern scholarship is divided on whether the unusual ending is deliberate (Magness 1986; Marcus 2009; Lincoln 1989 defend the deliberate-ending reading and document Hellenistic-Greek precedents for ending on *gar*) or the autograph's original ending was lost in transmission (Croy 2003) or the autograph was unfinished (Hooker 1991). See the central-glossary entry `mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-textual-critical-site` for the textual-critical apparatus.

paragraphs.text: Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ, παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια.
paragraphs.translit: Anastas de prōi prōtē sabbatou ephanē prōton Maria tē Magdalēnē, par’ hēs ekbeblēkei hepta daimonia.

i18n.en: Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

notes.official: **MAJOR TEXTUAL-CRITICAL SITE.** Mk 16:9-20 (the Longer Ending) is ABSENT in the earliest substantial witnesses (Codex Vaticanus B/03; Codex Sinaiticus א/01; Codex Bobiensis k Old Latin; Sinaitic Syriac). Consensus modern critical view (Metzger 1994 UBS Textual Commentary 102-106; Marcus AB 2009; Collins Hermeneia 2007; Croy 2003; Kelhoffer 2000) is that vv.9-20 is a 2nd-c. scribal addition composed to harmonize Mark with the resurrection-appearance narratives of Mt, Lk, and Jn. Internal-evidence case: 18 hapax legomena (words found nowhere else in Mark); the narrative awkwardly reintroduces Mary Magdalene as if for the first time (already named at 16:1). The WoH-Translation preserves the canonical longer-ending text on surface per the textual-critical convention; the dispute is documented in the central-glossary entry `mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-textual-critical-site` and the overlay-glossary entry `mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-rendering-convention`.

paragraphs.text: ἐκείνη πορευθεῖσα ἀπήγγειλεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ γενομένοις πενθοῦσι καὶ κλαίουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: ekeinē poreutheisa apēngeilen tois met’ autou genomenois penthousi kai klaiousin·

i18n.en: She went and told those who had been with him, as they were mourning and weeping.

paragraphs.text: κἀκεῖνοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ζῇ καὶ ἐθεάθη ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἠπίστησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kakeinoi akousantes hoti zē kai etheathē hyp’ autēs ēpistēsan.

i18n.en: And when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δυσὶν ἐξ αὐτῶν περιπατοῦσιν ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ πορευομένοις εἰς ἀγρόν·
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tauta dysin ex autōn peripatousin ephanerōthē en hetera morphē poreuomenois eis agron·

i18n.en: After these things, he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking, going into the country.

notes.official: The *ephanerōthē en hetera morphē* 'he appeared in another form' detail is a signature feature of the longer ending's harmonizing project: the verse compresses the Lukan Emmaus-walkers narrative (Lk 24:13-35) into a single sentence, with the *en hetera morphē* element accounting for the Emmaus-walkers' initial non-recognition of Jesus. The compression is one of the structural-features that flags the longer-ending block as a 2nd-c. compendium of other resurrection-appearance traditions.

paragraphs.text: κἀκεῖνοι ἀπελθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς λοιποῖς· οὐδὲ ἐκείνοις ἐπίστευσαν.
paragraphs.translit: kakeinoi apelthontes apēngeilan tois loipois· oude ekeinois episteusan.

i18n.en: And they went and told it to the rest; but they did not believe them either.

paragraphs.text: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀνακειμένοις αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ὠνείδισεν τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σκληροκαρδίαν ὅτι τοῖς θεασαμένοις αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν.
paragraphs.translit: Hysteron de anakeimenois autois tois hendeka ephanerōthē, kai ōneidisen tēn apistian autōn kai sklērokardian hoti tois theasamenois auton egēgermenon ouk episteusan.

i18n.en: Later he appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at table, and he rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who saw him after he had been raised.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα κηρύξατε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πάσῃ τῇ κτίσει.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois· Poreuthentes eis ton kosmon hapanta kēryxate to euangelion pasē tē ktisei.

i18n.en: And he said to them, "Go into all the world and proclaim the gospel to all creation.

paragraphs.text: ὁ πιστεύσας καὶ βαπτισθεὶς σωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ἀπιστήσας κατακριθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho pisteusas kai baptistheis sōthēsetai, ho de apistēsas katakrithēsetai.

i18n.en: The one who believes and is baptized will be saved, but the one who does not believe will be condemned.

paragraphs.text: σημεῖα δὲ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ταῦτα παρακολουθήσει· ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δαιμόνια ἐκβαλοῦσιν, γλώσσαις λαλήσουσιν καιναῖς,
paragraphs.translit: sēmeia de tois pisteusasin tauta parakolouthēsei· en tō onomati mou daimonia ekbalousin, glōssais lalēsousin kainais,

i18n.en: And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues;

notes.official: The Mk 16:17-18 'signs-catalogue' (demon-exorcism + glossolalia + serpent-handling + poison-immunity + sick-healing) is part of the textually-secondary longer-ending block. Kelhoffer 2000 *Miracle and Mission* surveys the patristic reception-history of the signs-catalogue and its functional role in the longer ending. The verse is engaged by the Raëlian canon (Raël 1975 *Extraterrestrials Took Me To Their Planet*) under the acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework documented at the central entry `mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-textual-critical-site`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν, κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ, ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tais chersin opheis arousin, kan thanasimon ti piōsin ou mē autous blapsē, epi arrōstous cheiras epithēsousin kai kalōs hexousin.

i18n.en: they will pick up serpents in their hands; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover.

notes.official: **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE** + reception-history of *en tais chersin opheis arousin* ('they will pick up serpents in their hands'). The verse is the textual basis for the small Appalachian serpent-handling tradition (Burton 1993 *Serpent-Handling Believers*; Kelhoffer 2000 surveys the patristic reception). Cross-reference to Acts 28:3-6 (Paul on Malta surviving the viper-bite) preserves the broader NT poison-immunity / serpent-handling tradition. The verse is part of the textually-secondary longer-ending block (ABSENT in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bobiensis + Sinaitic Syriac). The Raëlian canon engagement is acknowledged-without-endorsement per the established framework; see the overlay-glossary entry `mark-16-18-snake-handling-reception-history-convention` and the central-glossary entry `mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-textual-critical-site`.

paragraphs.text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν κύριος Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τὸ λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς ἀνελήμφθη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ho men oun kyrios Iēsous meta to lalēsai autois anelēmphthē eis ton ouranon kai ekathisen ek dexiōn tou theou.

i18n.en: So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

notes.official: **MAJOR RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE — THE MARKAN ASCENSION.** *anelēmphthē eis ton ouranon* 'was taken up into heaven' (Mk 16:19) is the Markan Ascension verse. Cross-corpus to Lk 24:51 + Acts 1:9-11 (the canonical Ascension narrative); *ek dexiōn tou theou* 'at the right hand of God' cross-corpus Ps 110:1 LXX, citing Mk 12:36 + 14:62. The verse is part of the textually-secondary longer-ending block (ABSENT in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bobiensis + Sinaitic Syriac). The Raëlian canon engagement (the Ascension read as the Elohim's departure-by-craft, Raël 1975 *Extraterrestrials Took Me To Their Planet*) is acknowledged-without-endorsement per the established framework. The compounding of the textual-critical layer (the verse is in a 2nd-c. scribal-addition block) with the Raëlian canon engagement is documented; see the central-glossary entries `mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-textual-critical-site` and `son-of-man-coming-in-cloud-dan-7-13-synoptic-revelation-1-7-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν πανταχοῦ, τοῦ κυρίου συνεργοῦντος καὶ τὸν λόγον βεβαιοῦντος διὰ τῶν ἐπακολουθούντων σημείων.
paragraphs.translit: ekeinoi de exelthontes ekēryxan pantachou, tou kyriou synergountos kai ton logon bebaiountos dia tōn epakolouthountōn sēmeiōn.

i18n.en: And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the signs that accompanied it.
